methodologyNotes: Twelve pasta makers spanning three mechanically distinct categories: fully automatic electric extruders (Philips HR2660/00, Philips HR2357/05, Emeril Lagasse Pasta & Beyond PM-01, Cuisinart PM-1 'Pastafecto', Ronco Electric Pasta Maker, GVODE Electric Pasta Maker), a stand-mixer attachment (KitchenAid KSMPRA), and manual hand-crank rollers (Marcato Atlas 150, Imperia SP150, CucinaPro 150, Weston 01-0201, Shule 6-in-1). Primary sources are official manufacturer spec sheets/manuals (Philips PDF datasheets; the Tristar/Emeril and Cuisinart owner's manuals) and, where manufacturer sites blocked automated access or lacked current US pricing, established US kitchenware retailers (Sur La Table, WebstaurantStore, Newegg) plus a 24-retailer price aggregator (ShopSavvy) for the discontinued Cuisinart model. 'roller_width_mm' and 'thickness_settings' apply only to machines with an adjustable sheet-forming roller (manual-crank models and the KitchenAid attachment); both are null for extrusion-style automatic makers, which force dough through fixed-shape discs instead of rolling sheets. 'motorized' is true whenever the roller/auger is driven by any electric motor — a unit's own built-in motor, or (for the KitchenAid attachment) the host stand mixer's motor — and false only for genuine hand-crank machines; 'wattage' is null for the KitchenAid attachment (it draws from whichever mixer it's mounted on) and for any electric unit whose wattage could not be confirmed from a credible source. Seed corrections: 'Philips Pasta Maker Plus HR2660' was corrected — Philips' own literature names this model simply the '7000 series Pasta Maker'; 'Pasta Maker Plus' is Philips' name for the unrelated HR2375 line. 'CucinaPro 150' was confirmed to be Imperia's own 'Home Pasta Machine 150' mechanism, imported and rebadged by CucinaPro (model CCP-4100) for US retail — its thickness-setting count is carried over from the verified-identical Imperia unit and flagged as such in its provenance rather than independently sourced. The roster was expanded from the 10 seeds to 12 by adding a second Philips model (HR2357/05, a smaller/older automatic unit still turning up in 2026 buyer comparisons) and a Weston manual roller. 'Gvode' is corrected to the brand's own capitalization, GVODE. Where a credible USD price, wattage, dishwasher-safety claim, or product image could not be independently verified, the field is left null (or the image key omitted) rather than estimated — this affects price for the Ronco and Shule entries, wattage for the KitchenAid, Cuisinart, CucinaPro, Weston, GVODE and Shule entries, and images for the Ronco and Shule entries. All web sources were accessed 2026-08-01.

products.name: Philips 7000 Series Pasta Maker HR2660/00
products.priceNote: Philips does not publish a direct USD MSRP on usa.philips.com; price reflects a Walmart.com listing for the same HR2660/00 SKU (checked 2026-08).

specs.dies_included: spaghetti, fettuccine, penne, lasagna, angel hair, thick spaghetti
specs.material: Plastic and metal outer/inner housing; metal mixing paddle and front-panel bar

products.provenance: Official Philips spec sheet (HR2660/00, issue date 2024-02-01) confirms 200W, 700g dough capacity, 6 shaping discs included in the box (spaghetti, fettuccine, penne, lasagna, angel hair, thick spaghetti — four more shapes are sold as separate accessories), non-stick dishwasher-safe parts, dimensions 32.2x22.9x32.7cm, weight 6.81kg, and plastic+metal construction. A parallel US SKU, HR2660/03, also exists (150W, 8 discs per its own Philips page); this entry documents the /00 variant matching the seed's spec sheet. Seed name 'Pasta Maker Plus' corrected: Philips' own naming for this model is simply the '7000 series Pasta Maker' — 'Pasta Maker Plus' is the name Philips uses for the unrelated HR2375 line. Release year 2024 is approximated from the spec sheet's issue date (2024-02-01); Philips does not publish an official launch date. Nella Online (US foodservice retailer) independently corroborates the 6 discs, capacity, and ProExtrude/automatic operation, and shows the closest available USD-adjacent pricing (CAD-listed there); the $265.00 figure used here reflects a Walmart.com listing for the same SKU found via search.

products.name: Philips Premium Collection Pasta and Noodle Maker HR2357/05
products.priceNote: Appears discontinued/out of stock at every US retailer checked (Newegg: listed with no price, out of stock; Best Buy and Amazon product pages returned server errors on repeated fetch attempts) as of 2026-08-01.

specs.material: Plastic main body and accessories; aluminum bar with PTFE coating

products.provenance: Official Philips spec sheet (HR2357/05, issue date 2023-04-20) confirms 200W/120V, 4 default shaping discs (spaghetti, penne, fettuccini, lasagna), dimensions 343x215x300mm, weight 7.5kg (product only), and a plastic main body with an aluminum+PTFE-coated kneading bar. The sheet lists a one-push 'cleaning tool' but never states the parts are dishwasher-safe — unlike the newer HR2660 sheet, which explicitly does — so dishwasher_safe_parts is recorded false. Newegg's listing independently confirms model identity, 200W, 4 discs, and near-identical dimensions (16in x 13.4in x 12in), lists it as out of stock with no current price, and supplied the verified product image. Release year 2023 is approximated from the spec sheet's issue date.

products.name: Marcato Atlas 150 Pasta Machine
products.priceNote: Sur La Table US listing price.

specs.material: Nickel- and chrome-plated steel with ABS plastic components

products.provenance: Sur La Table's US listing confirms $199.95, nine adjustable dial thickness settings (0.8-4mm), chrome/nickel-plated-steel plus ABS construction, and hand-wash-only care (explicitly not dishwasher safe). Interismo.com (an EU retailer) independently corroborates the 150mm roller width, a 10-position dial (positions 0-9, i.e. nine clicks matching Sur La Table's 'nine settings'), anodised-aluminum rollers with polymer-resin scrapers, and manual hand-crank operation, and its product photo was verified as a genuine JPEG via direct fetch (used here as the image). The base Atlas 150 ships with an integrated, easy-to-remove double cutter that produces fettuccine and tagliolini (confirmed on the Sur La Table listing), so those two are recorded in dies_included; the additional shapes (spaghetti, lasagnette, ravioli, bigoli, trenette, etc.) are sold as separate paid Marcato attachments and are excluded here.

products.name: Imperia Home Pasta Machine SP150
products.priceNote: Sur La Table US listing price.
products.provenance: Sur La Table confirms $149.95, a 150mm (5.9in) roller, a built-in double cutter producing fettuccine and tagliolini, steel/aluminum/plastic/rubber/beechwood construction, and hand-wash-only care ('do not immerse'). Danish retailer H.W. Larsen independently corroborates six adjustable thickness settings, a stainless-steel build, the same built-in Duplex Cutter (tagliatelle/fettuccine), and gives dimensions 185x160x205mm and weight 3.8kg for the SP150. Unlike the Marcato Atlas 150, Imperia's SP150 includes its cutter dies as standard equipment rather than as a separate accessory.

products.name: KitchenAid 3-Piece Pasta Roller & Cutter Set (KSMPRA)
products.priceNote: WebstaurantStore listing price; street price varies widely by retailer (e.g. Best Buy ~$183.99, Home Depot ~$204.90 per search-indexed listings not independently fetched).
products.provenance: WebstaurantStore confirms $249.95 and chrome-plated-steel construction for KitchenAid's 3-piece Pasta Roller & Cutter Set (one roller, one fettuccine cutter, one spaghetti cutter, plus a cleaning brush; formerly sold as the KPEX). Independently indexed retailer descriptions consistently describe a 6-inch (152mm) roller with 8 thickness settings and hand-wipe-only cleaning (not dishwasher safe), though those specific retailer pages (Home Depot, Best Buy, Everything Kitchens) returned 403/timeout errors on direct fetch and are cited only as background, not as a formal corroboration source. This is a stand-mixer attachment, not a self-powered unit: 'motorized' is recorded true because the roller/cutters are driven by the KitchenAid stand mixer's motor rather than a hand crank; wattage is null because the attachment itself has no motor or wattage rating of its own — it depends entirely on whichever mixer model it is mounted on.

products.name: Emeril Lagasse Pasta & Beyond (PM-01)

specs.dies_included: tagliatelle, spaghetti, fettuccine, penne, angel hair, linguine, lasagne, udon
specs.material: Plastic housing with a metal auger and kneading paddle

products.provenance: The official Tristar Products owner's manual (Model PM-01, distributed by Tristar Products Inc., Fairfield NJ) confirms 120V/60Hz, 150W rated power, a 1 lb pasta capacity (two-batch program equals 1 lb; one batch equals 1/2 lb), and 8 included pasta discs — Tagliatelle, Spaghetti, Fettuccine, Penne, Angel Hair, Linguine, Lasagne, Udon (the Spaghetti disc ships pre-installed; the rest store in the base's storage tray) — and states in Cleaning & Storage that 'the parts and other accessories are durable and dishwasher safe' (the motor base itself must never be submerged). Retailer emerillagassestore.com corroborates the model and lists it at $189.99, and supplied the product image. Emeril Pasta & Beyond is a multi-function base whose meat-grinder, slicer/shredder, slow-juicer, and frozen-treat housings are sold separately; only the pasta-making configuration is recorded here.

products.name: Cuisinart PM-1 Pastafecto Pasta & Bread Dough Maker
products.priceNote: Discontinued directly by Cuisinart. ShopSavvy's 24-retailer aggregate (updated 2026-08-02) showed a $80.99 (Amazon) to $256.11 range; $80.99 is used here as the representative current low.

specs.dies_included: bucatini, spaghetti, fusilli, rigatoni, small macaroni, fettuccine
specs.material: Plastic housing and mixing bowl with a metal kneading paddle

products.provenance: Cuisinart's own product page for the PM-1 'Pastafecto' now lives at a URL beginning '/discontinued-pastafecto-...' and 404s, confirming discontinuation. The Cuisinart owner's manual (via ManualsLib) confirms a 1 lb pasta / 1 lb bread-dough capacity and 6 pasta discs (bucatini, spaghetti, fusilli, rigatoni, small macaroni, fettuccine), and states 'all detachable parts are dishwasher safe.' Wattage could not be confirmed from any manufacturer-authored source reached; a low-trust dropship listing (martdiscover.com) claims 250W and lists the unit at $349.99 — a price far outside the $80-256 range independently aggregated by ShopSavvy across 24 retailers — so that site's figures are treated as unreliable and wattage is left null rather than repeated. martdiscover.com's product photo was verified as a genuine JPEG via direct fetch and used as the image despite the site's unreliable pricing.

products.name: CucinaPro-Imperia Home Pasta Machine 150 (CCP-4100)
products.priceNote: Street price commonly cited around $80-100 (smartpastamaker.com); one clearance retailer (todaysconcept.com) listed it at $61.99 (regular $72.99), marked 'no longer available' there.
products.provenance: Multiple independent US kitchenware retailers (kidstoolsshop, bestcookstore, cafeteks, bestkitchendining, todaysconcept, Everything Kitchens) sell this literally as the 'CucinaPro-Imperia Home Pasta Machine 150' / model CCP-4100 — i.e. the same Imperia-manufactured mechanism as Imperia's own 'Home Pasta Machine 150' (a sibling of the SP150 reviewed separately in this dataset), imported and rebadged by CucinaPro for US retail. todaysconcept.com confirms a 6-inch roller, chrome-plated steel, and a built-in double cutter head for spaghetti and fettuccine, and supplied the verified product image; smartpastamaker.com's hands-on review independently corroborates the 6-inch roller, chrome plating, and double cutter, and gives the $80-100 street price. thickness_settings (6) is carried over from the confirmed-identical Imperia mechanism, since no CucinaPro-branded page states the count directly — flagged here rather than silently sourced as if independently verified for this SKU.

products.name: Ronco Electric Pasta, Noodle and Sausage Maker
products.priceNote: No verifiable current USD price found: ronco.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt this session, and the Walmart listing required human CAPTCHA verification to view.
products.provenance: The Ronco Electric Pasta Maker's owner's manual (via ManualsLib) confirms 120V/60Hz operation, 180W max, five interchangeable attachments, and states 'all accessories (apart from the motor unit!) are dishwasher-safe.' Ronco's own site (ronco.com) could not be reached — every attempt this session returned HTTP 429 — so the current official model number, exact disc/shape names, housing material, and price could not be confirmed from the manufacturer; product identity is anchored instead to a Walmart listing titled 'Ronco Electric Pasta, Noodle and Sausage Maker Kitchen Machine, White,' which itself could not be fetched past its bot-check page. dies_included and material are left null rather than guessed since no accessible source named them. No usable product image could be retrieved (Amazon and manual-hosting sites returned only stylesheets/scripts or HTTP 403s), so the image field is omitted rather than filled with a placeholder.

products.name: GVODE Electric Pasta Maker Machine, 3-in-1 Roller & Cutter Set
products.priceNote: lovablekitchen.com review price ($84.99); third-party marketplace reseller (apasmak.com) shows a much wider $135.98-$213.99 range, likely inflated dropship pricing.
products.provenance: The Amazon listing title confirms product identity verbatim: 'GVODE Electric Pasta Maker Machine, 3-in-1 Pasta Roller & Cutter Set, White | Adjustable Thickness Settings for Fresh Spaghetti, Fettuccine, Lasagna Sheets with Compact Storage and Easy Cleanup.' A 2026 review (lovablekitchen.com) independently states 8 adjustable thickness levels (0.4-2mm), a 150mm roller, aluminum construction, hand-wash-only care (not dishwasher safe), and a $84.99 price, and its cited product photo resolves to a genuine Amazon CDN JPEG (verified by direct fetch), used here as the image. The same review's claim of a '700W max motor' is not corroborated anywhere else, is implausible for a compact countertop roller/cutter of this type (compare: Philips' fully automatic dough-extruding pasta makers run only 150-200W), and sits alongside an unrelated, likely templated claim on the same page that the unit is 'KitchenAid stand-mixer compatible' (the Amazon title describes a standalone electric unit, not an attachment) — both read as generic review-site noise, so wattage is left null rather than repeating an unverified figure.

products.name: Weston Traditional Style Pasta Machine (01-0201, 'Roma')
products.priceNote: WebstaurantStore listing price; that retailer marks the listing 'no longer available' but it is the only price figure confirmed by direct fetch (a True Value listing for the same model number showed $36.99 in search results, not independently verified here).
products.provenance: WebstaurantStore's listing for the 'Weston 01-0201 Roma Manual Traditional Style Pasta Machine' confirms a 6-inch (152mm) stainless-steel roller, 7 thickness settings, a built-in fettuccine/spaghetti double cutter, a C-clamp for countertop mounting, and lists it at $31.49 (marked no longer available at that retailer), and supplied the verified product image. Weston's own site (westonbrands.com) returned only empty content across repeated fetch attempts, and Walmart/Best Buy/eBay listings for the same model were blocked by bot-check pages or timeouts, so dishwasher-safety could not be confirmed from the manufacturer and is left null rather than assumed from other manual machines in this dataset.

products.name: Shule 6-in-1 Manual Pasta Maker Machine
products.priceNote: No verifiable current USD price found: Amazon serves this listing's price only via client-side JavaScript that automated fetching could not render, and manufacturer shulegroup.com is a China-based OEM/export site with no consumer US pricing.
products.provenance: The Amazon listing's title and bullet points (independently reconfirmed across two separate fetch attempts) describe a stainless-steel manual pasta machine with 7 adjustable roller thickness settings (0.5-3mm) producing a 150mm-wide sheet, plus two fixed cutting blades for vermicelli (1.5mm) and fettuccine (6.6mm). Shule's manufacturer site (shulegroup.com) confirms the brand makes a family of manual 150mm pasta machines (models QF-150, QZ-150, SLK-150) for OEM/private-label export, but does not expose consumer pricing or state which model corresponds to this specific Amazon SKU. No price or product image could be retrieved because Amazon renders both via client-side JavaScript not present in the fetched HTML, and a direct browser-header curl request was served Amazon's generic bot-check shell rather than the product page; the image key is therefore omitted rather than filled with a guess.
